title: Operator purges jobs in bulk by site, status, or age
description:
Single-hash operations do not scale to real cleanup. Retiring a publisher,
clearing out every job from a backend that generated badly, or dropping
everything failed after an incident are all per-job loops today -- and before
the delete story lands, they are impossible at any scale.

Deliberately lower priority than the single-job stories: bulk delete is the
most destructive operation in the product and should be built on routes that
have already proven themselves.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Bulk job cleanup

  Scenario: Operator previews a bulk delete before running it
    Given twelve jobs exist for site "site-a"
    When the operator previews a bulk delete for site "site-a"
    Then the response reports twelve matching jobs
    And no jobs are deleted

  Scenario: Operator deletes every failed job
    Given three jobs exist with status "failed"
    And two jobs exist with status "done"
    When the operator bulk deletes jobs with status "failed"
    Then the three failed jobs are removed
    And the two done jobs remain

  Scenario: Operator deletes jobs older than a cutoff
    Given a job created ninety days ago
    And a job created today
    When the operator bulk deletes jobs older than thirty days
    Then only the ninety day old job is removed

  Scenario: Bulk delete removes audio objects
    Given three jobs exist with status "done" and stored audio objects
    When the operator bulk deletes jobs with status "done"
    Then all three audio objects are removed from the audio bucket

  Scenario: Bulk delete requires at least one filter
    When the operator bulk deletes with no filter
    Then the response is a bad request
    And no jobs are deleted
```

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`**

- Route: `POST /admin/jobs/bulk-delete` -> `_bulk_delete_admin_jobs(body, headers)`.
  A POST, not a DELETE: it carries a filter body and must never be reachable
  by accident.
- Body: `{"site_id": str?, "status": str?, "older_than_days": int?, "dry_run": bool}`.
  At least one of the three filters is required -- an unfiltered bulk delete
  wipes the table and must raise `ValueError`.
- Default `dry_run` to `True`. The caller opts in to destruction explicitly.
- Reuse the paging already written for `_list_admin_jobs` (including the
  `status-created_at-index` GSI) to select matches; do not write a second
  scan path.
- Delete S3 objects with `delete_objects` in batches of up to 1000 rather than
  one call per job, and `batch_writer()` for the table.
- Return `{"matched": int, "deleted": int, "dry_run": bool}`.
- Cap a single call (1000 jobs) and return a continuation token rather than
  risking a Lambda timeout mid-delete.

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** — `bulk_delete_jobs(...)`.

**`cli/src/auritus/commands/job.py`** — `auritus job purge` with `--site`,
`--status`, `--older-than-days`, and `--yes`. Without `--yes` it runs the
dry run, prints the match count, and prompts.

**Console** — out of scope. Bulk destruction stays on the CLI for now.

## Blocked on

The delete story, whose S3-plus-record semantics this reuses.

comments.text: Implemented on feature/admin-bulk-purge, merged to develop. POST /admin/jobs/bulk-delete, dry_run defaults True, at least one of site_id/status/older_than_days required or ValueError->400. Status-filtered path reuses _query_jobs_by_status (cheap); site/age-only filters have no matching GSI (only status-created_at-index and claimed_by-index exist) and honestly documented as reading the whole table via _query_jobs_by_status across all statuses rather than silently scanning -- flagged a dedicated site_id GSI as a fast-follow if this gets used at scale. Capped at 1000 matches per call with a truncated flag. Extracted _delete_job_record_and_audio as the shared deletion core so bulk delete doesn't redundantly re-fetch/re-auth per item the way looping over the single-delete route would. auritus job purge in the CLI: always previews first, requires --yes to proceed, re-confirms interactively. Independently re-verified: reverted the fix myself and confirmed all 5 scenarios genuinely fail (including the 'requires a filter' scenario specifically returning 404 pre-fix vs 400 post-fix, not a coincidental status match). Full suite green: black/ruff, pytest (59 passed), behave (27 features, 103 scenarios).
